<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.3in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimated fair value of stock is the closing market price of the Company&#146;s common stock on the date of warrant issuance and end of each reporting period the derivative instruments are marked to market. Expected volatility is based on historical volatility of Synergy&#146;s common stock. The warrants have a transferability provision and based on guidance provided in SAB&nbsp;107 for instruments issued with such a provision, Synergy used the full contractual term as the expected term of the warrants. The risk free rate is based on the U.S. Treasury security rates for maturities consistent with the expected remaining term of the warrants. Expected volatility is based on historical volatility of the Company&#146;s common stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.3in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<td width="3%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:3.0%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>
<td width="19%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:19.2%;">
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">0%</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.2%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.3in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the Binomial model, the assumption for estimated fair value of the stock is based on a Black-Scholes based apportionment of the unit price paid for the shares and warrants issued in Synergy&#146;s most recent registered direct offerings, which resulting stock prices were deemed to be arms-length negotiated prices.&nbsp;Expected volatility is based on historical volatility of Synergy&#146;s common stock. The warrants have a transferability provision and based on guidance provided in SAB&nbsp;107 for instruments issued with such a provision, Synergy used the full contractual term as the expected term of the warrants. The risk free rate is based on the U.S. Treasury security rates for maturities consistent with the expected remaining term of the warrants.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The unrealized gains or losses on the derivative liabilities are recorded as a change in fair value of derivative liabilities in the Company&#146;s statement of operations. A financial instrument&#146;s level within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of any input that is significant to the fair value measurement. At each reporting period, the Company reviews the assets and liabilities that are subject to ASC Topic 815-40. At each reporting period, all assets and liabilities for which the fair value measurement is based on significant unobservable inputs or instruments which trade infrequently and therefore have little or no price transparency are classified as Level 3.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">6. Stockholders&#146; deficit</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;28, 2011 and March&nbsp;8, 2011 Callisto entered into consulting agreements with two financial advisors who agreed to receive an aggregate of 850,000 shares of Callisto common stock, with a fair value of $533,000, as full compensation for their services, which has been recorded as prepaid expense and $308,000 has been amortized over the term of the agreements for the nine months ended September 30, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:21.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February 19, 2011 a Callisto warrant holder exercised his warrant to purchase 106,667 shares of Callisto common stock at an exercise price of $0.50 per share yielding gross proceeds of $53,334.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:21.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March 4, 2011, Synergy closed a registered direct offering with a non-U.S. investor which raised gross proceeds of $1,800,000. Synergy issued to the investor 300,000 shares of its Synergy common stock and warrants to purchase 210,000 shares of Synergy common stock. The purchase price paid by the investor was $6.00 for each unit. The warrants expire after seven years and are exercisable at $6.20 per share. Based upon the Company&#146;s analysis of the criteria contained in ASC Topic 815-40, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#151;Contracts in Entity&#146;s Own Equity&#148; Synergy has determined that the warrants issued in connection with this Financing transaction must be recorded as derivative liabilities upon issuance and marked to market on a quarterly basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From May&nbsp;2 to May&nbsp;23, 2011, Synergy entered into securities purchase agreements with certain investors to raise gross proceeds of $2,499,999 in a registered direct offering.&nbsp; Synergy issued to the investors 416,667 shares of its Synergy common stock and warrants to purchase 416,667 shares of Synergy common stock. The purchase price paid by the investors was $6.00 for each unit. The warrants expire after seven years, are exercisable at $4.25 per share and the exercise price is protected, in the event of subsequent equity sales at a lower price, for a period of two years from issuance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon the Company&#146;s analysis of the criteria contained in ASC Topic 815-40, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#151;Contracts in Entity&#146;s Own Equity&#148; Synergy has determined that the warrants issued in connection with this Financing transaction must be recorded as derivative liabilities upon issuance and marked to market on a quarterly basis. &#160;These liabilities in the amount of $725,000 were reclassed on December&nbsp;19, 2011 to additional paid in capital.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June 3, 2011, a Synergy warrant holder exercised his warrants and purchased a total of 80,000 shares of Synergy common stock. &#160;Synergy raised gross proceeds of $415,309 as a result of the warrant exercise. &#160;The purchase price paid by the warrant holder was $5.00 for 49,383 shares and $5.50 for 30,617 shares. Based upon the Company&#146;s analysis of the criteria contained in ASC Topic 815-40, Synergy had determined that the warrants exercised in connection with this transaction were derivative liabilities when issued and the Company had been marking this liability to market at the end of each reporting period.&nbsp;Upon the exercise of these warrants the fair value of the related derivative liability totaling $486,328 was reclassified to Additional Paid in Capital.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From June 3 to June&nbsp;15, 2011, Synergy entered into securities purchase agreements with certain investors to raise gross proceeds of $1,161,243 in a private placement.&nbsp; Synergy issued to the investors 193,541 shares of Synergy common stock and warrants to purchase</font></p>

Based upon the Company&#146;s analysis of the criteria contained in ASC Topic 815-40, Synergy has determined that the warrants issued in connection with this private placement must be recorded as derivative liabilities upon issuance and marked to market on a quarterly basis. <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The October&nbsp;4, 2011 transaction pricing resulted in the exercise price of the 416,667 warrants issued during May&nbsp;2011 (the &#147;May Warrants&#148;) to be reduced to $4.25 per share of Synergy common stock. The &#147;price protection&#148; rights attributable to the May Warrants remain in effect until the Company&#146;s listing on NASDAQ, December 1, 2011. This exercise price reduction from $6.50 per share to $4.25 per share decreased the prospective exercise proceeds attributable to the May Warrants by $937,500.</font></p>

The Warrants expire after five years and are exercisable at $5.50 per share. &#160;Based upon the Company&#146;s analysis of the criteria contained in ASC Topic 815-40, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#151;Contracts in Entity&#146;s Own Equity&#148; Synergy has determined that the investor warrants issued in connection with this Financing transaction must be recorded as derivative liabilities upon issuance and marked to market on a quarterly basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December 1, 2011, Synergy entered into an underwriting agreement for the public offering and sale of 1,875,000 units, consisting of two shares of Synergy common stock and one warrant to purchase one share of Synergy common stock. On December 6, 2011 Synergy closed the offering at a price of $8.00 per unit, resulting in gross proceeds to the Company of $15,000,000. &#160;Each warrant has an exercise price of $5.50 per share and will expire five years from the date of issuance. &#160;Synergy also granted the Underwriters, under the terms of the Underwriting Agreement, an option to purchase up to an additional 281,250 units to cover over-allotments. &#160;On December&nbsp;15, 2011 the over-allotment option was exercised for additional gross proceeds of $2,250,000. &#160;Based upon the Company&#146;s analysis of the criteria contained in ASC Topic 815-40, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#151;Contracts in Entity&#146;s Own Equity&#148; Synergy has determined that warrants issued in connection with this Financing transaction were not derivative liabilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December 6, 2011, in connection with this underwritten financing, Synergy issued a total of 112,500 common stock purchase options to the underwriters and several principals of the firm. The Options expire three years from issuance and have an exercise price of $5.00 per share. Based upon the Company&#146;s analysis of the criteria contained in ASC Topic 815-40, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#151;Contracts in Entity&#146;s Own Equity&#148; Synergy has determined that the warrants issued in connection with this Financing transaction were not derivative liabilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, Synergy paid $2,148,383 in selling agent fees and legal expenses related to the above financing transactions and issued 9,025 warrants to a selling agent which expire after seven years and are exercisable at $6.50 per share, and 77,750 units consisting of one share of Synergy common stock and one warrant to purchase one share of Synergy common stock, which expire in five years, and are exercisable at $5.50 per share.&nbsp; Based upon the Company&#146;s analysis of the criteria contained in ASC Topic 815-40, Synergy has determined that 8,025&nbsp;warrants issued to selling agents were equity instruments upon issuance and 78,750 warrants must be recorded as derivative liabilities upon issuance and marked to market on a quarterly basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 Synergy issued a total of 79,000 shares of Synergy common stock in payment for legal, consulting and scientific advisory services rendered.&nbsp; The fair value of these shares totaled $341,295 which amount has been reflected in our statement of operations for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;29, 2010, Callisto entered into a Note and Warrant Exchange Agreement with the holders of its Secured Promissory Notes due April 30, 2011 (the &#147;Notes&#148;), which were issued in December&nbsp;2008 along with the related Callisto common stock purchase warrants exercisable for 68,883,536 shares of common stock (the &#147;Warrants&#148;), pursuant to which such holders exchanged the Notes plus accrued interest and the Warrants for an aggregate 72,355,770 shares of Callisto common stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying value of the Notes extinguished, including accrued but unpaid interest, was $709,639. In accordance with ASC Topic 405-20 Callisto calculated the difference between (i)&nbsp;the fair value of the Warrants received plus the carrying value of Notes extinguished and (ii)&nbsp;the fair value of the common stock issued to the note and warrant holders. This resulted in a loss of $2,099,892 on extinguishment of the debt, which was recorded in the statement of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;30, 2010, the price protection provision included in the New Warrants expired. As a result, we measured the fair value of the outstanding warrants as of June&nbsp;30, 2010, recognized any changes in value in earnings and then reclassified the derivative instrument liability into stockholder&#146;s equity.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;22, 2010, Callisto reached an agreement with more than the requisite holders of 70% of the outstanding $603,163 principal amount of 11% Secured Promissory Notes due April&nbsp;15, 2010 (the &#147;Notes&#148;) to extend the due date of the Notes to April 30, 2011. In exchange for the amendment, the Company agreed to issue to the note holders 15% of the amount of principal and interest due on the Notes as of March 31, 2010 payable in shares of common stock, or 265,770 shares of common stock. This modification of debt was considered &#147;substantially different&#148; and was accounted for as a modification of debt. The carrying value of the notes payable before</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-24<a name="PB_24_085511_3020"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">modification in the amount of $647,606 was extinguished and the fair value of the new debt in the amount $671,103 was recorded. The fair value of the shares totaled $100,196 which cost was recorded as a loss on extinguishment during the three months ended March&nbsp;31, 2010 and included in interest and other expense in the statement of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;30, 2008, Callisto entered into a securities purchase and exchange agreement (&#147;Purchase Agreement&#148;) with several investors, each of whom were holders of record as of November&nbsp;4, 2008 of outstanding warrants to purchase shares of the Company&#146;s common stock, exercisable at $0.50 or $0.70 per share until August&nbsp;2, 2010 (&#147;Series&nbsp;B Warrants&#148;). The Series&nbsp;B Warrants were issued in connection with the private placement of the Company&#146;s Series&nbsp;B Preferred Shares on August&nbsp;2, 2007. During the period from December&nbsp;30, 2008 to June&nbsp;17, 2009, pursuant to the Purchase Agreement, Callisto issued $603,163 principal amount of 11% Secured Notes due April&nbsp;15, 2010 (&#147;11% Notes&#148;). Interest on the 11% Notes is due at maturity and repayment of the 11% Notes is secured by a pledge of up to 2,292,265 shares of the common stock of Synergy owned by Callisto. Pursuant to the Purchase Agreement, Callisto issued 69,086,174 common stock purchase warrants (&#147;New Warrants&#148;) in exchange for the surrender and cancellation of 26,938,800 outstanding Series&nbsp;B Warrants. The New Warrants have an exercise price, subject to certain anti-dilution adjustments, of $0.02 per share and are exercisable at any time on or prior to December&nbsp;31, 2016. In connection with the issuance of $349,880 of the $603,163 11% Notes in June&nbsp;2009, Callisto entered into an additional security agreement granting all of the holders of the 11% Notes&nbsp;a security interest in the Atiprimod technology acquired by the Company in December&nbsp;2008.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:26.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The proceeds from the issuance of these instruments were allocated to the 11% Notes and the New Warrants based upon the relative fair values of the 11% Notes and the New Warrants. The New Warrants had a fair value of $6,781,471 upon issuance, measured utilizing the Black Scholes fair value methodology using assumptions ranging from 7.5 to 8&nbsp;years for expected term, volatility of 150% to 200%, no dividends and risk free interest rates ranging from 1.76% to 3.33%. This resulted in a debt discount of $552,728 apportioned to the New Warrants which was being accreted to the 11% Notes as interest expense over the life of the 11% Notes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;30, 2010, Synergy entered into securities purchase agreements to sell securities to non-U.S. investors and raised gross proceeds of approximately $2,754,000 in a registered direct offering. Synergy sold 324,000 units at $8.50 per share to investors. Each unit consists of one share of Synergy&#146;s common stock and one warrant to purchase one additional share of Synergy&#146;s common stock. The warrants expire after five years and are exercisable at $9.00 per share. The offering was made pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form&nbsp;S-3 (the base prospectus effective December&nbsp;10, 2009), as supplemented by a prospectus supplement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on June&nbsp;23, 2010. As of June&nbsp;30, 2010, Synergy had received proceeds of $255,000, less legal fees of $25,000 associated with this offering. The remaining $2,499,000 was held in escrow and received by Synergy on July&nbsp;2 and July&nbsp;8, 2010. In July&nbsp;2010, the Company paid an aggregate $261,630 to selling agents in connection with this placement. In accordance with ASC 815-40, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#151;Contracts in Entity&#146;s Own Equity&#148; the warrants have been classified as a derivative liability.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;16, 2010, Synergy entered into a securities purchase agreement with an accredited investor to sell securities and raise gross proceeds of $400,000 in a private placement. The Company sold 49,383 units to the investor with each unit consisting of one share of the Synergy common stock and one warrant to purchase one additional share of Synergy&#146;s common stock. Synergy paid a fee of $33,000 to a non-US selling agent and $7,500 in legal expenses on this placement. The purchase price paid by the investor was $8.10 for each unit. The warrants expire after five years and are exercisable at $8.50 per share. In accordance with ASC 815-40, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#151;Contracts in Entity&#146;s Own Equity&#148; the warrants have been classified as a derivative liability.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;1, 2010, Synergy entered into a securities purchase agreement with an investor and raised gross proceeds of $2,500,000 in a registered direct offering. The Company paid a fee of $50,000 to a non-U.S. selling agent. Synergy sold to the investor 500,000 shares of Synergy common stock and warrants to purchase 200,000 shares of Synergy common stock. The Synergy common stock and warrants were sold in units consisting of one share of Synergy&#146;s common stock and two-fifths of a warrant to purchase a share of Synergy&#146;s common stock. The purchase price paid by the investor was $5.00 for each unit. The warrants expire after five years and each whole warrant has an exercise price of $5.50 per share. In accordance with ASC 815-40, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#151;Contracts in Entity&#146;s Own Equity&#148; the warrants have been classified as a derivative liability.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;16, 2009, the Company amended the Series&nbsp;A and Series&nbsp;B Convertible Preferred Stock to eliminate the liquidation preference and decrease the conversion price of the Series&nbsp;A and B Convertible Preferred Stock to $0.36 per share from $0.50 per share. The closing price of the Company&#146;s common stock on September&nbsp;16, 2009 was $0.20 per share. The additional shares of Callisto common stock, valued at the share price on the date of the modification, have been accounted for as a dividend on the Series&nbsp;A and B Convertible Preferred Stock totaling $136,889 and $1,678,703, respectively, during the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;14, 2008, Callisto entered into an Exchange Agreement dated July&nbsp;11, 2008 (&#147;Exchange Agreement&#148;), as amended and effective on July&nbsp;14, 2008, with Pawfect Foods,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Pawfect&#148;), Synergy Pharmaceuticals,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Synergy-DE&#148;), a majority-owned subsidiary of Callisto, and other holders of Synergy-DE common stock according to the terms of the Exchange Agreement, Pawfect acquired 100% of the common stock of Synergy-DE, from Callisto and the other holders of Synergy-DE, in exchange for 22,732,380 shares of Pawfect&#146;s common stock representing approximately 70% of Pawfect&#146;s outstanding common stock (the &#147;Exchange Transaction&#148;). Callisto received 22,295,000 of the 22,732,380 shares of Pawfect&#146;s common stock exchanged for its ownership of Synergy-DE, and Callisto is now the holder of 68% of Pawfect&#146;s outstanding common stock. The remaining 437,380 shares of Pawfect common stock exchanged for ownership of Synergy-DE were issued to certain executive officers of Synergy-DE who received their shares pursuant to a Repurchase Agreement with Synergy-DE dated July&nbsp;3, 2008 and assumed by Pawfect. The fair value of each of the 437,380 shares was estimated on the grant date to be $1.20, which was based on the price paid by shareholders participating in Synergy&#146;s July&nbsp;14, 2008 private placement. Stock based compensation expense of $524,856 related to these shares is being amortized over the vesting period of 2&nbsp;years. In connection with the Exchange Transaction Pawfect received $3,025,000 less transaction costs of $73,087, yielding net proceeds of $2,951,913 from two private placements, which the Company has recorded as an increase in additional paid-in capital.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;7, 2008, Callisto received notice from the staff of the American Stock Exchange (&#147;AMEX&#148;) of its intent to strike Callisto&#146;s common stock from the AMEX by filing a delisting application with the SEC for failure to regain compliance with Sections&nbsp;1003(a)(i)&nbsp;and 1003(a)(ii)&nbsp;of the Company Guide and falling out of compliance with Section&nbsp;1003(a)(iii)&nbsp;of the Company Guide with shareholders&#146; equity of less than $6,000,000 and losses from continuing operations and/or net losses in four of our five most recent fiscal years. On July&nbsp;14, 2008, Callisto&#146;s common stock was delisted from the AMEX and currently trades on the Over The Counter Bulletin Board under the Symbol CLSP.OB.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;31, 2008, the Board of Directors approved a reassignment, as well as, a decrease in the exercise price, of the 1,323,822 warrants, previously assigned from Trilogy Capital Partners&nbsp;LLC to two unaffiliated entities, from $1.03 per share to $0.70 per share. The decrease in the exercise price was effective immediately and the reassignment will be effective at management&#146;s discretion. Callisto has determined that the price modifications was compensatory in accordance with ASC 718 and the associated stock-based compensation expense of $45,086 was recorded during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;27, 2007, Callisto filed a Certificate of Amendment to its Certificate of Incorporation increasing its authorized number of shares of common stock from 150,000,000 to 225,000,000. The Certificate of Amendment was approved by Callisto&#146;s stockholders at its annual meeting on September&nbsp;26, 2007. On March&nbsp;2, 2007, at a Special Meeting of Stockholders of the Corporation, the stockholders voted to amend the Callisto&#146;s Certificate of Incorporation, as amended, to increase the number of authorized shares of common stock, par value $.0001 per share, from 100,000,000 shares to 150,000,000 shares.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During August&nbsp;2007, Callisto closed a private placement of 1,147,050 shares of Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock and 22,941,000 Warrants to certain Investors for aggregate gross proceeds of $11,470,500 pursuant to a Securities Purchase Agreement dated as of August&nbsp;2, 2007. Each share of Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock was immediately convertible into that number of shares of common stock determined by dividing the stated value of $10.00 of such share of Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock by $0.50, at the option of the holder, at any time and from time to time. The Warrants are immediately exercisable at $0.70 per share at any time within three years from the date of issuance. In connection with this transaction, Callisto paid aggregate fees and expenses of $920,960 and issued warrants to purchase 2,518,900 shares of common stock exercisable at $0.50 per share at any time within three years from the date of issuance and 2,518,900 shares of common stock exercisable at $0.70 per share at any time within four years from the date of issuance to certain selling agents. The fair value of the selling agent warrants on the date of grant was $1,839,962 using Black Scholes assumptions of 60% volatility, a risk free interest rate of 4.57% to 4.31%, no dividend, an expected life of 4&nbsp;years and a stock price on the dates of grant ranging from $0.66 to $0.68 per share. This fair value was accounted for as a cost of capital.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, 10,000 shares of Series&nbsp;B Convertible Preferred Stock were converted to 200,000 shares of common stock at a conversion price of $0.50 per share. There were no conversions of the Series&nbsp;B Convertible Preferred Stock during the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2007.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other than pursuant to certain issuances, for the twelve month period beginning on the effective date of the Registration Statement registering the resale of the shares of Common Stock underlying the Warrants by the Holder, if the Company at any time while the Warrants are outstanding, shall sell or grant any option to acquire shares of Common Stock, at an effective price lower than the then exercise price then, the exercise price shall be reduced to such lower price.</font></p>

The Investors also are parties to a Registration Rights Agreement, dated as of August&nbsp;2, 2007 pursuant to which the Company agreed to file, within 45&nbsp;days of closing, a registration statement covering the resale of the shares of common stock underlying the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock and Warrants issued to the Investors. Failure to file&nbsp;a registration statement and maintain its effectiveness as agreed will result in the Company being required to pay liquidated damages equal to 1% per month of the aggregate purchase price paid by the Investors, not to exceed an aggregate of 18%. The Company filed a Form&nbsp;S-3 Registration Statement covering the sale of the common shares underlying the conversion of the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock and the Warrants on September&nbsp;11, 2007 and this Form&nbsp;S-3 was declared effective by the SEC on September&nbsp;27, 2007.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Voting Rights.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock shall have no voting rights. However, so long as any shares of Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock are outstanding, the Company shall not, without the affirmative vote of the holders of the shares of the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock then outstanding, (a)&nbsp;alter or change adversely the powers, preferences or rights given to the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock or alter or amend the Certificate of Designation (whether by merger, consolidation or otherwise), (b)&nbsp;authorize or create any class of stock ranking as to dividends, redemption or distribution of assets upon a Liquidation senior to or otherwise <i>pari passu</i> with the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock, (c)&nbsp;amend its certificate of incorporation or other charter documents so as to affect adversely any rights of the holders, (d)&nbsp;increase the authorized number of shares of Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock, or (e)&nbsp;enter into any agreement with respect to the foregoing.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Liquidation.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon any liquidation, dissolution or winding-up of the Company, whether voluntary or involuntary, the holders shall be entitled to receive out of the assets of the Company, whether such assets are capital or surplus, for each share of Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock an amount equal to the stated value of $10.00 per share, plus any accrued and unpaid dividends thereon and any other fees or liquidated damages owing thereon before any distribution or payment shall be made to the holders of any junior securities, and if the assets of the Company shall be insufficient to pay in full such amounts, then the entire assets to be distributed to the Holders shall be distributed among the holders ratably in accordance with the respective amounts that would be payable on such shares if all amounts payable thereon were paid in full.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Conversions at Option of Holder.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Each share of Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock shall be convertible into that number of shares of common stock determined by dividing the stated value of $10.00 of such share of Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock by $0.50 (the &#147;Conversion Price&#148;), at the option of the holder, at any time and from time to time.</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">volume of the common stock is at least 0.5% of the shares that are being converted, the Company shall have the right to convert any portion of the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock into shares of common stock at the then-effective Conversion Price.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Subsequent Equity Sales.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For the twelve (12)&nbsp;month period beginning on the effective date of the registration statement registering the resale of the shares of common stock underlying the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock by the holder, if the Company at any time while Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock is outstanding, shall sell or grant any option to purchase or otherwise dispose of or issue any common stock or common stock equivalents entitling any Person to acquire shares of Common Stock, at an effective price per share less than the then Conversion Price (the &#147; <i>Base Conversion Price</i> &#147;), then, the Conversion Price shall be reduced to an amount equal to the Base Conversion Price.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As per ASC Topic 480, &#147;Accounting for Certain Financial Instruments with Characteristics of Both Liabilities and Equity&#148;, the Company determined the balance sheet classification of the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock to be equity given that the mandatory redemption option had expired as of September&nbsp;30, 2007. The escrow was released on October&nbsp;1, 2007 with no further claims or restrictions on the cash.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As per ASC Topic 815, &#147; <i>Accounting for Derivative Financial Instruments Indexed to, and Potentially Settled in, Company Stock</i> &#147;, Callisto has determined that the fair value of the Series&nbsp;B Warrants issued to the Lead Investors should be treated as a liability upon issuance and reclassified to permanent equity based on the fair value upon expiration of the Put Option. The change in fair value of the Series&nbsp;B Lead Investor warrant from the date of issuance through the expiration of the Put Option was recorded as other income totaling $2,591,005 during the three and nine months ended September&nbsp;30, 2007. Callisto has determined that the warrants issued to other than Lead Investors should be treated as &#147;permanent equity&#148;.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As per ASC Topic 825 &#147;Accounting for Registration Payment Arrangements&#148;, issued in December&nbsp;2006, which specifies that contingent obligations under a registration payment arrangement should be separately recognized and measured in accordance with ASC Topic 450 &#147; <i>Accounting for Contingencies</i> &#147;. Callisto has determined that no liability needed to be recorded because the Company filed a timely registration statement covering the sale of the common shares underlying the conversion of the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock and the Warrants on September&nbsp;11, 2007.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As per ASC Topic 470, &#147;Debt&#148; Callisto evaluated the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock transaction and accordingly found that there was an embedded beneficial conversion feature. The fair value of the detachable warrants on the date of grant was $6,677,513 using Black Scholes assumptions of 60% volatility, a risk free interest rate of 4.57% to 4.31%, no dividend, an expected life of 3&nbsp;years and a stock price on that dates of grant ranging from $0.66 to $0.68 per share. The conversion rights of the Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock contained an embedded beneficial conversion feature totaling $10,495,688 that was immediately accreted to the Series&nbsp;B Convertible Preferred Stock as a dividend because the preferred stock could be converted immediately upon issuance.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From October&nbsp;23, 2006 until January&nbsp;10, 2007, Callisto placed 602,350 shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock and 8,031,333 warrants to certain investors for aggregate gross proceeds of $6,023,500. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 Callisto had closed on 574,350 shares of such Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock for aggregate gross proceeds of $5,743,500. The final tranche of this financing closed January&nbsp;10, 2007 when Callisto placed 28,000 shares of such Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock for aggregate gross proceeds of $280,000. The shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock are convertible into shares of common stock at a conversion price of $0.75 per share. The investors also are parties to a Registration Rights Agreement, dated as of October&nbsp;23, 2006 pursuant to which Callisto agreed to file, within 60&nbsp;days of closing, a registration statement with the SEC covering the resale of the shares of common stock underlying the Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock and the warrants issued to the investors. The warrants are immediately exercisable at $0.75 per share, will expire five years from the date of issuance, and have certain anti-dilution rights for the twelve month period beginning on the effective date of the registration statement registering the shares of common stock underlying the warrants. Callisto (i)&nbsp;paid aggregate fees and expenses of $485,308 ($448,908 prior to December&nbsp;31, 2006) in cash and (ii)&nbsp;issued an aggregate 11,775 shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock and 1,228,761 warrants to purchase common stock, to certain selling agents. The warrants are immediately exercisable at $0.75 per share, will expire five years after issuance and have the same anti-dilutive rights as the investor warrants. The fair value of the selling agent warrants on the date of grant was $640,481 using Black Scholes assumptions of 60% volatility, a risk free interest rate of 4.60%, no dividend, an expected life of 5&nbsp;years and a stock price on the dates of grant of $0.88 per share. This fair value was accounted for as a cost of capital.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:26.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The material terms of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock consist of:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Dividends.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Holders of the Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock shall not be entitled to receive dividends except as and if declared at Callisto&#146;s sole election.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Voting Rights.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Shares of the Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock shall have no voting rights. However, so long as any shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock are outstanding, Callisto shall not, without the affirmative vote of a majority in interest of the shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock then outstanding, (a)&nbsp;alter or change adversely the powers, preferences or rights given to the</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-29<a name="PB_29_090037_7091"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock, (b)&nbsp;authorize or create any class of stock senior or equal to the Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock, (c)&nbsp;amend its articles of incorporation or other charter documents, so as to affect adversely any rights of the holders of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock or (d)&nbsp;increase the authorized number of shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Liquidation.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Subject to the rights of the holders of the Series&nbsp;B Convertible Preferred Stock, upon any liquidation, dissolution or winding-up of Callisto, the holders of the Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock shall be entitled to receive an amount equal to the Stated Value per share, which is $10 per share plus any accrued and unpaid dividends.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Conversion Rights.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Each share of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock shall be convertible into that number of shares of common stock determined by dividing the Stated Value, currently $10 per share, by the conversion price, currently $0.36 per share. The conversion price is subject to adjustment for dilutive issuances.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Automatic Conversion.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Beginning October&nbsp;24, 2007, if the price of the common stock equals $1.50&nbsp;per share for 20 consecutive trading days, and an average of 50,000 shares of common stock per day shall have been traded during the 20 trading days, Callisto shall have the right to deliver a notice to the holders of the Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock, to convert any portion of the shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock into shares of Common Stock at the conversion price.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As per ASC Topic 815, Callisto has determined that the warrants should be treated as &#147;permanent equity&#148;.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As per ASC Topic 825, which specifies that contingent obligations under a registration payment arrangement should be separately recognized and measured in accordance with FASB ASC Topic 450 &#147;Accounting for Contingencies&#148;, Callisto has determined that no liability needed to be recorded. On January&nbsp;12, 2007 Callisto filed a registration statement on Form&nbsp;S-3 registering the common stock issuable upon (i)&nbsp;the conversion of the all Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock, (ii)&nbsp;the exercise of all related investor warrants and (iii)&nbsp;the exercise of all selling agent warrants. On February&nbsp;15, 2007 Amendment No.1 to this registration statement was declared effective by the SEC.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As per ASC Topic 470, Callisto evaluated the Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock transaction and accordingly found that there was an embedded beneficial conversion feature. The fair value of the detachable warrants on the date of grant was $3,557,872 using Black Scholes assumptions of 60% volatility, a risk free interest rate of 4.57% to 4.84%, no dividend, an expected life of 5&nbsp;years and a stock price on that dates of grant ranging from $0.88 to $0.75 per share. The conversion rights of the Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock issued during the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2006 contained a beneficial conversion feature totaling $2,384,485. This beneficial conversion feature was immediately accreted to the Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock as a dividend because the preferred stock could be converted immediately upon issuance. The beneficial conversion feature associated with final tranche of 28,000 shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock placed on January&nbsp;10, 2007 amounted to $119,685 and was recorded as a beneficial conversion feature accreted as a dividend in the quarter ended March&nbsp;31, 2007.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:26.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock and Warrants issued from October&nbsp;23, 2006 through January&nbsp;10, 2007 have certain anti-dilution rights. As a result of the August&nbsp;2, 2007 Series&nbsp;B Preferred Stock financing the conversion price of the then remaining Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock and the exercise price of the then remaining Series&nbsp;A Warrants was reset from $0.75 per share to $0.50 per share. This modification resulted in $2,384,790 of additional beneficial conversion accreted as a dividend during the quarter ended September&nbsp;30, 2007. The total beneficial conversion feature accreted as a dividend for the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2007 and 2006 was $2,504,475 and $2,384,485, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2007, 36,125 shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock were converted to 481,666 shares of common stock prior to August&nbsp;2, 2007 at a conversion price of $0.75 per share and 359,325 shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock were converted to 7,186,500 shares of common stock subsequent to August&nbsp;2, 2007, at a conversion price of $0.50 per share. During the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, 120,675 shares of Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock were converted to 2,413,500 shares of common stock at a conversion price of $0.50 per share.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;8, 2006 Callisto entered into a Letter Agreement with certain investors (the &#147;Investors&#148;) who participated in a private placement of our common stock and warrants in February&nbsp;and April&nbsp;2006 (the &#147;Prior Placement&#148; see below). Pursuant to this Letter Agreement, the Investors agreed to amend (the &#147;Amendment&#148;) the securities purchase agreement (the &#147;Securities Purchase Agreement&#148;), entered into in connection with the Prior Placement, to (i)&nbsp;delete the mandatory registration rights set forth in the Securities Purchase Agreement and add piggyback registration rights and (ii)&nbsp;waive any unpaid penalties pursuant to the liquidated damages provisions contained in the Securities Purchase Agreement. In addition, the Investors agreed to enter into a lock-up agreement (the &#147;Lock-up Agreement&#148;) pursuant to which they agreed not to sell or transfer the shares of common stock and warrants acquired in the Prior Placement for a period of nine months beginning September&nbsp;1, 2006. In exchange for the Investors entering into the Amendment and the Lock-Up Agreement, Callisto agreed to issue to each Investor one share of common stock and 2.35 five year warrants exercisable at $1.00 per share (the &#147;New Warrants&#148;) for every five shares of common stock they purchased in the Prior Placement. In addition, Callisto agreed in the Letter Agreement to amend the warrants (the &#147;Old Warrants&#148;) issued in the Prior Placement to the Investors to (i)&nbsp;extend the </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">7. Share-based payments</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Callisto Pharmaceuticals,&nbsp;Inc. Stock Option Plans</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 1996, Callisto adopted the 1996 Incentive and Non-Qualified Stock Option Plan (the &#147;Plan&#148;) for employees, consultants and outside directors to purchase up to 2,000,000 shares of common stock. This Plan was amended in December&nbsp;2002 to increase the number </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-32<a name="PB_32_090659_7906"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">of shares authorized under the Plan to 10,000,000. The option term for the 3,113,817 options outstanding as of December&nbsp;31, 2011 under the Plan is ten years from date of grant. The Plan terminated on January&nbsp;1, 2006 under its original terms and no further options will be granted under the Plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;20, 2005, Callisto stockholders approved the 2005 Equity Compensation Incentive Plan. The maximum number of shares of common stock with respect to which awards may be granted under the 2005 Equity Plan is 5,000,000. The option term for options granted under the 2005 Equity Plan is ten years from date of grant and there were 2,770,000 options available for future grants as of December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;20, 2005, Callisto stockholders approved our 2005 Directors&#146; Stock Option Plan. The maximum number of shares of common stock with respect to which awards may be granted under the 2005 Directors&#146; Plan is 1,000,000. The option term for options granted under the 2005 Directors&#146; Plan is ten years from date of grant and there are 833,000 options shares available for future grants as of December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:26.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The options Callisto grant under the 2005 Equity Plan may be either &#147;incentive stock options&#148; within the meaning of Section&nbsp;422 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#147;Code&#148;), or non-statutory stock options at the discretion of the Board of Directors and as reflected in the terms of the written option agreement. None of our stock option plans are qualified deferred compensation plans under Section&nbsp;401(a)&nbsp;of the Code, and are not subject to the provisions of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (ERISA). As of December&nbsp;31, 2011, Callisto has 1,924,555 stock options outstanding not subject to our stock option plans.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Stock Option Accounting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004, the FASB issued ASC Topic 718 (Revised 2004), <i>Share-Based Payments</i> (&#147;ASC Topic 718&#148;). This guidance requires companies to measure the cost of employee services received in exchange for the award of equity instruments based on the estimated fair value of the award at the date of grant. The expense is to be recognized over the period during which an employee is required to provide services in exchange for the award.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ASC Topic 718 did not change the way Callisto account for non-employee stock-based compensation. Callisto continues to account for shares of common stock, stock options and warrants issued to non-employees based on the fair value of the stock, stock option or warrant, if that value is more reliably measurable than the fair value of the consideration or services received. Stock-based compensation expense associated with these non-employee option grants is being recorded in accordance with ASC Topic 505 and accordingly (i)&nbsp;the measurement date will be when &#147;performance commitment is completed&#148; and accordingly the fair value of these options is being &#147;marked to market&#148; quarterly until the measurement date is determined.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ASC Topic 718 requires that cash flows resulting from tax deductions in excess of the cumulative compensation cost recognized for options exercised (excess tax benefits) be classified as cash inflows from financing activities and cash outflows from operating activities. Due to Callisto&#146;s accumulated deficit position, no tax benefits have been recognized in the cash flow statement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Callisto accounts for common stock, stock options, and warrants granted to non-employees based on the fair market value of the instrument, using the Black-Scholes option pricing model based on assumptions for expected stock price volatility, term of the option, risk-free interest rate and expected dividend yield at the grant date.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:4.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Callisto Share-Based Compensation</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock options issued by Callisto typically vest after three years of continuous service from the grant date and have a contractual term of ten years. The fair values are amortized to share-based compensation pro-rata over the vesting term.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Share-based payments have been recognized in operating results as follow:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:26.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The estimated fair value of each employee and non-employee stock option award was determined on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option valuation model with the following weighted-average assumptions during the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, 2010 and 2009.</font></p>

<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.42%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Risk-free interest rate</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &#151;Based upon observed US Treasury security interest rates appropriate for the expected term of Callisto&#146;s employee stock options.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Dividend yield</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &#151;Callisto has not paid any dividends on common stock since its inception and does not anticipate paying dividends on its common stock in the foreseeable future.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Expected volatility</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &#151;Based on the historical volatility of Callisto&#146;s stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Expected term</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &#151;Callisto has had no stock options exercised since inception. The expected option term represents the period that stock-based awards are expected to be outstanding based on the simplified method provided in ASC 718, &#147;Share-Based Payment&#148;, (&#147;ASC 718&#148;) which averages an award&#146;s weighted-average vesting period and expected term for &#147;plain vanilla&#148; share options. Under SAB No.&nbsp;107, options are considered to be &#147;plain vanilla&#148; if they have the following basic characteristics: (i)&nbsp;granted &#147;at-the-money&#148;; (ii)&nbsp;exercisability is conditioned upon service through the vesting date; (iii)&nbsp;termination of service prior to vesting results in forfeiture; (iv)&nbsp;limited exercise period following termination of service; and (v)&nbsp;options are non-transferable and non-hedgeable. In December&nbsp;2007, the SEC issued SAB110, <i>Share-Based Payment</i> . This guidance was effective January&nbsp;1, 2008 and expresses the views of the Staff of the SEC with respect to extending the use of the simplified method, as discussed in ASC 718, in developing an estimate of the expected term of &#147;plain vanilla&#148; share options in accordance with ASC 718. The Company will continue to use the simplified method until it has the historical data necessary to provide a reasonable estimate of expected life. For the expected term, the Company has &#147;plain-vanilla&#148; stock options, and therefore used a simple average of the vesting period and the contractual term for options granted subsequent to January&nbsp;1, 2006.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Forfeitures</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &#151;ASC Topic 718 requires forfeitures to be estimated at the time of grant and revised, if necessary, in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates. Callisto estimated future unvested option forfeitures based on historical Company experience and has incorporated this rate in determining the fair value of employee option grants.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:26.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The weighted-average fair value of all options granted under Callisto&#146;s Plans during the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, 2010 and 2009, estimated as of the grant date using the Black-Scholes option valuation model, was $0.49, $0.19 and $0.15 per share, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:26.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The unrecognized compensation cost related to Callisto&#146;s non-vested employee stock options outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010 was $26,852 and $45,193, respectively, to be recognized over a weighted-average vesting period of approximately 1 year and 2 years, respectively. The weighted-average remaining term of all options outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2011 was 1.2 years as compared to 4.2&nbsp;years at December&nbsp;31, 2010.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ASC Topic 718 requires that cash flows resulting from tax deductions in excess of the cumulative compensation cost recognized for options exercised (excess tax benefits) be classified as cash inflows from financing activities and cash outflows from operating activities. Due to the Company&#146;s accumulated deficit position, no tax benefits have been recognized in the cash flow statement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Synergy Stock Option Plan</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:4.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock Options</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ASC Topic 718 <i>&#147;Compensation&#151;Stock Compensation&#148;</i> requires companies to measure the cost of employee services received in exchange for the award of equity instruments based on the estimated fair value of the award at the date of grant. The expense is to be recognized over the period during which an employee is required to provide services in exchange for the award. ASC Topic 718 did not change the way Synergy accounts for non-employee stock-based compensation. Synergy continues to account for shares of common stock, stock options and warrants issued to non-employees based on the fair value of the stock, stock option or warrant, if that value is more reliably measurable than the fair value of the consideration or services received. The Company accounts for stock options issued and vesting to non-employees in accordance with ASC Topic 505-50 &#147;Equity <i>-Based Payment to Non-Employees&#148;</i> and accordingly the value of the stock compensation to non-employees is based upon the measurement date as determined at either a)&nbsp;the date at which a performance commitment is reached, or b)&nbsp;at the date at which the necessary performance to earn the equity instruments is complete. Accordingly the fair value of these options is being &#147;marked to market&#148; quarterly until the measurement date is determined.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ASC Topic 718 requires that cash flows resulting from tax deductions in excess of the cumulative compensation cost recognized for options exercised (excess tax benefits) be classified as cash inflows from financing activities and cash outflows from operating activities. Due to Synergy&#146;s accumulated deficit position, no excess tax benefits have been recognized. Synergy accounts for common stock, stock options, and warrants granted to employees and non-employees based on the fair market value of the instrument, using the Black-Scholes option pricing model based on assumptions for expected stock price volatility, term of the option, risk-free interest rate and expected dividend yield, at the grant date.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Synergy adopted the 2008 Equity Compensation Incentive Plan (the &#147;Plan&#148;) during the quarter ended September&nbsp;30, 2008. Stock options granted under the Plan typically vest after three years of continuous service from the grant date and have a contractual term of ten years. Synergy did not issue stock options prior to the quarter ended September&nbsp;30, 2008.&nbsp;Stock-based compensation expense related to Synergy options and restricted stock units have been recognized in operating results as follow:</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
